text:
Maya (SRE): Follow-up from the postmortem: multiple private deployments flagged intermittent RPC failures tied to VPC peering. Pattern: MTU/fragmentation + occasional asymmetric return path. Need owners, short remediation steps, and a weekly check to catch regressions.

Liam (Eng-Platform): I can take ownership of the peering validation checks and the weekly regression job. Will add a lightweight health-check that verifies MTU and reassembly. ETA: Tue next week.

Ivy (Private Deploy): I'll own code-level mitigations in the on-prem adapter (MSS clamping and conservative handshake retries). Can target a small patch this sprint. Need test vectors from customers who hit it.

Carlos (CSE): I'll collate the affected customer list and send sample pcap captures we have. Also will coordinate with their network teams for evidence collection. Expect to have artifacts by tomorrow lunchtime.

Maya (SRE): Minimal oncall play I want in runbook:
- quick triage steps (ping/traceroute/mtu-path)
- when to flip to dedicated fallback route (criteria + approver)
- links to debug scripts and ticket INC-4902

Liam (Eng-Platform): Draft quick commands (to be added to runbook):
```bash
# check path MTU
sudo ping -M do -s 1472 -c 3 10.1.2.3
# confirm reassembly allowed
tcpdump -n -s 0 'host 10.1.2.3 and (ip[6:2] & 0x3fff != 0)'
# verify peering status (aws example)
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active
```
I'll post a PR with the health-check script that runs these and reports fail/pass to the infra dashboard.

Ivy (Private Deploy): Note: some on-prem boxes silently drop fragments. If we detect fragmented packets from captures, we should enable MSS clamping server-side and advise customer to change device config. Patch will include an opt-in flag in the agent config.

infra-bot: INC-4902 created: "private-peering-mtu-frag-investigation". Assigned to: Maya, Liam, Ivy. Priority: P2.

Carlos (CSE): Customer A has provided a pcap showing many fragmented packets and duplicate ACKs. Uploading to INC-4902 now.

Maya (SRE): Thanks. Action slate:
- Liam: add regression job + runbook snippet (ETA Tue)
- Ivy: adapter patch + canary plan (ETA end of sprint; expedite if pcap confirms)
- Carlos: collect remaining pcaps and device configs (ETA tomorrow)
- Maya: add escalation matrix and dedicated fallback play (ETA Fri)

Liam (Eng-Platform): Quick Q: should the health-check live in infra-monitoring or private-deploy repo? I prefer infra-monitoring so it can run as a scheduled probe across all regions.

Ivy (Private Deploy): Agree infra-monitoring. But please add a webhook so private-deploy can trigger a local agent check when we roll a patch.

Carlos (CSE): Customer B reported similar symptoms last month. I'll link INC-4737 and note the overlap in patterns. Looks like a recurring incident class worth tracking weekly.

Maya (SRE): Good catch. Let's add a recurring label "peering-mtu" on INC-4902 and schedule a 15m sync every Wednesday until we have <2% of private deployments affected.

Liam (Eng-Platform): :thumbsup: starting PR for the checker now: internal link: https://git.redwood.internal/infra-monitoring/pulls/91

Ivy (Private Deploy): :thumbsup: will draft agent opt-in config + unit tests.

Carlos (CSE): :thumbsup: collecting pcaps and contacting customer infra.

Maya (SRE): If anyone is blocked, call it out here. We'll treat this as the canonical remediation thread and update INC-4902.

(END)
